rationale: The current competition-specific Kaggle metadata limits CPU and GPU submissions to 540 minutes. ARC3 therefore fails closed at 32400 seconds, which is stricter than the generic 12-hour notebook ceiling, and protects 6000 seconds for startup, framework, scorecard closure, and artifact emission. Dynamic allocations cap any one game at 240 seconds while reserving at least 5 seconds and one action for each future environment. The 10-second controller-call ceiling bounds the measured apply-consequence plus next-decision production cycle, including sparse recovery checkpoints; the tournament governor's smaller remaining slice still controls near a game deadline.
